title: improv·artist · sound (Janet Cardiff)
mutation_directive: improv artist: sound via Janet Cardiff

improv_extras.practice: binaural sound walks; 40-part motet; spatial audio as place

v1.feedback: The two-column speaker sources with a wave-interference field between them is a legit translation of Cardiff's 40-part motet spatial principle — the idea clearly drove the geometry, not just the comments. The standing-wave brightness modulation gives readable structure: you can see constructive/destructive bands, which is good. However the form reads as a rectangular volume of flickering dots flanked by two thin pillars — it's more 'physics demo' than 'installation presence.' To push it: curve the field particles into a cathedral-nave or elliptical plan (Cardiff's motet was in a specific chapel), let the interference nodes coalesce into denser filaments rather than just alpha-modulating a uniform grid, and consider a very slow camera drift (simulating the listener's walk) so the phase pattern visibly shifts without user input. Palette is restrained and appropriate but could use one warm accent at peak constructive interference to give the eye a focal reward.

v2.feedback: The 40-voice interference pattern is a genuinely clever translation of Cardiff's 40-Part Motet into particle space — constructive/destructive nodes create visible filaments that read as 'sound made solid,' and the elliptical nave plan with cypress-taper columns gives architectural legibility within 2 seconds. The slate-to-amber palette is restrained and the warm peaks reward the eye at interference maxima. To refine: the field particles between columns still read a bit cloudy/nebular in destructive zones — push destructive alpha closer to zero so the filament ridges pop harder against true black, making the standing-wave geometry unmistakable. The slow elliptical camera walk is good but could occasionally pause or breathe near a column cluster to let the viewer 'lock in' to a voice group, mirroring the spatial listening experience Cardiff designs for.
